title: Sleigh Chase: The first 16-bit console game coded by AI (open source)
author: javierprieto
selftext:
Hi there!

We are a small retro development duo based in Seville and Malaga (Spain). After creating a few games for Spectrum and Mega Drive, and while we continue working on our main project, The Weave, we wanted to create a special Christmas and New Year greeting for the holidays in the form of three minigames for the Sega Mega Drive/Genesis: Sleigh Chase.

[https://geese-bumps.itch.io/sleigh-chase](https://geese-bumps.itch.io/sleigh-chase)

   
**In-game screens:**

https://preview.redd.it/75atwi2sef9g1.png?width=640&format=png&auto=webp&s=7ae1424cd5ca5ea034ea2c16aec77d3a1ee2be26

https://preview.redd.it/q1z4wsitef9g1.png?width=640&format=png&auto=webp&s=9fe2a69e2e17134d560dc2ffb2573e1708d391e0

https://preview.redd.it/d6yo2jfuef9g1.png?width=640&format=png&auto=webp&s=0c3376415f3fae8c280df725086c343adab57b00

What makes this project unique is that it was programmed entirely using OpenAI’s Codex, making it—to the best of our knowledge—the first 16-bit console game with code fully generated by AI. The only handcrafted part is the music, composed by Haddhar.

You can download the game on our Itch page, and the full source code and assets are available on GitHub (the project is completely open source): [https://github.com/Ganso/Sleigh-Chase](https://github.com/Ganso/Sleigh-Chase)

I have also prepared a detailed post explaining the development process and the tools I used, as a contribution to the community for anyone interested in replicating our work (only available in Spanish by now, but AI powered translators work just fine, you know 😉): [https://geese-bumps.itch.io/sleigh-chase/devlog/1151152/creando-sleigh-chase-desarrollo-para-mega-drive-acelerado-con-ia](https://geese-bumps.itch.io/sleigh-chase/devlog/1151152/creando-sleigh-chase-desarrollo-para-mega-drive-acelerado-con-ia)

Regards!

comments.author: ELPascalito
comments.body: Did GPT Image 1.5 generate the art? And may I ask what compilers you used? What does "fully made by AI" exactly mean, because I truly believe the human direction is what matters in such projects

replies.author: javierprieto
replies.body:
I really encorage you to read the traslated version of my devlog:  
[https://geese-bumps.itch.io/sleigh-chase/devlog/1151152/creando-sleigh-chase-desarrollo-para-mega-drive-acelerado-con-ia](https://geese-bumps.itch.io/sleigh-chase/devlog/1151152/creando-sleigh-chase-desarrollo-para-mega-drive-acelerado-con-ia)

I did not use GPT Image 1.5. I used Nano Banana to generate high-resolution concepts, which I then manually adapted, animated, and optimized in Aseprite to fit the Mega Drive's 16-color palettes and VRAM limits. The pixel work was largely hands-on to ensure hardware compatibility. For the code, I used OpenAI Codex to generate C functions for the SGDK compiler, managing the AI like a junior developer through GitHub pull requests, while the music was entirely human-composed by Haddhar using DefleMask.

When I say "fully made by AI," I mean that while I didn't type the source code myself, I acted as the Project Director. I defined every mechanic, tuned the gameplay, and guided the AI through the specific hardware constraints. The AI executed the technical implementation, but the creative vision, game design, and quality control were 100% human-driven—much like a film director guiding a crew rather than operating the camera themselves.

All the project was done in about two weeks of my litte spare time. Most mechanics were coded by the mobile version of Codex and later mergeed and tested by me.

comments.author: javierprieto
comments.body:
TLDR of the Devlog. Generative AI use in the project:

OpenAI Codex – Generated 100% of the C code for SGDK. I wrote zero lines of code myself; Codex handled all implementation based on my detailed specifications and iterative feedback through GitHub pull requests.

Nano Banana – High-resolution concept art and visual ideation. Output: Initial graphics (later manually adapted in Aseprite for pixel art and hardware optimization).

Eleven Labs – Text-to-speech for sound effects and voice lines. Output: final SFX samples and UI audio (no editing needed)

Key Point: I acted as Project Director—defining mechanics, reviewing code changes, tuning gameplay constants, and optimizing assets—but I did not write a single line of code. Codex generated all the source code; my role was architectural direction, testing, and validation.

comments.author: Wow_Crazy_Leroy_WTF
comments.body: Is there a video? I don’t wanna play it but I’d love to watch it

replies.author: Wow_Crazy_Leroy_WTF
replies.body:
Thanks! My 2 cents:

We see too little in front of the sleigh (which is quite big). Either the sleight needs to be smaller or we need to zoom out (so that the sleigh is smaller and we see more in front of it). 

Alternatively, if the sleigh moves left to right, you would gain more screen space because of the aspect ratio (wide screen has more width than height). 

But maybe it doesn’t matter. Maybe it’s just an AI showcase as opposed to a moneymaking venture. 

I am impressed. Good job.

replies.author: javierprieto
replies.body:
Thanks for your comments 

As a matter of fact, I used a vertical scrolling mini game as a template, so it was easier doing it so. I had very very little time to make the game, so I tried to reuse as many functions as possible, so making both vertical and horizontal scrolling levels was not possible 

If I did it again I'd surely make some changes, as the one you are suggesting. By now, it's just a quick minigame and tech demo, as well as my Christmas and New Year congratulation for both the retro and vibe coding communities :)
